physics_goals.quote: The NA38 and NA50 experiments at the CERN SPS have measured charmonium production in different colliding systems with the aim of observing a phase transition from ordinary hadronic matter towards a state in which quarks and gluons are deconfined
physics_goals.value: Observe a phase transition from ordinary hadronic matter to a state in which quarks and gluons are deconfined, by measuring charmonium (J/psi) suppression

summary.plain: NA50 was a CERN experiment that fired lead ions at lead targets and counted pairs of muons from J/psi particles. It found that J/psi production in central collisions was unexpectedly low, an effect called anomalous J/psi suppression and seen as a sign of quark-gluon plasma.
summary.technical: NA50: dimuon spectrometer with beam hodoscope, three centrality detectors (neutral transverse-energy calorimeter, zero-degree calorimeter, multiplicity detector) and a hadron absorber measuring J/psi and Drell-Yan dimuons in Pb-Pb collisions at 158 GeV per nucleon (and p-A at 450 GeV) at the SPS North Area, 1995-2000; follow-up to NA38; found J/psi suppression beyond normal nuclear absorption.

unique_capabilities.quote: The NA50 apparatus consists essentially of a set of beam and anti-halo counters, three centrality detectors, and a muon spectrometer.
unique_capabilities.value: Dimuon spectrometer with centrality detectors measuring J/psi and Drell-Yan production in Pb-Pb collisions
